questions.stem: This Giemsa-stained thick blood smear shows an elongated, sheathed larval organism coiling among the red cells. What is this organism?

explanation.summary: Microfilariae of W. bancrofti are small larval nematodes seen in thick blood smears stained with Giemsa; they circulate in the blood with nocturnal periodicity.
explanation.whyCorrect: Microfilariae of W. bancrofti are small larval nematodes seen in thick blood smears stained with Giemsa; they circulate in the blood with nocturnal periodicity.

questions.stem: This Giemsa-stained thick blood smear from a febrile traveler shows a long, coiled, sheathed larva among the red cells. Detection of this organism confirms infection with which parasite?

explanation.summary: A peripheral blood smear stained with Giemsa demonstrating sheathed microfilariae is the most straightforward way to identify W. bancrofti.
explanation.whyCorrect: A peripheral blood smear stained with Giemsa demonstrating sheathed microfilariae is the most straightforward way to identify W. bancrofti.

questions.stem: This thick blood smear stained with Giemsa demonstrates a single elongated sheathed microfilaria. Given this organism's periodicity, when should the blood sample ideally be collected?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Early in the morning at waking

choices.label: C
choices.text: At night, around 10 PM to 2 AM

choices.label: D
choices.text: At any random time of day

explanation.summary: W. bancrofti microfilariae are nocturnal, so blood collected at night (approximately 10 PM to 2 AM) yields the highest diagnostic sensitivity.
explanation.whyCorrect: W. bancrofti microfilariae are nocturnal, so blood collected at night (approximately 10 PM to 2 AM) yields the highest diagnostic sensitivity.

questions.stem: Panel (a) shows marked conjunctival redness without purulent discharge and panel (b) shows oral mucosal hemorrhage in a systemically ill patient. These findings are most characteristic of severe disease caused by which organism?

explanation.summary: Conjunctival suffusion is a hallmark of leptospirosis, and severe (Weil) disease can produce hemorrhage such as the oral bleeding shown here.
explanation.whyCorrect: Conjunctival suffusion is a hallmark of leptospirosis, and severe (Weil) disease can produce hemorrhage such as the oral bleeding shown here.

questions.stem: This patient shows gross enlargement, hyperkeratosis, and thickening of the lower leg due to long-standing lymphatic obstruction. What is the most likely underlying infection?

explanation.summary: Advanced elephantiasis of the limb reflects irreversible lymphatic fibrosis and destruction from chronic W. bancrofti infection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Advanced elephantiasis of the limb reflects irreversible lymphatic fibrosis and destruction from chronic W. bancrofti infection.
